name: Tranylcypromine
metabolism: Evidence is from Tranylcypromine 10 mg film-coated tablets (oral). Tranylcypromine is well and rapidly absorbed after oral administration, with peak plasma levels reached after about 2.5 hours and a half-life of the order of 2 hours. It undergoes considerable metabolism, including breakdown of the side chain and probably conjugation. Its main action is irreversible inhibition of MAO, both MAO-A and MAO-B; this lasts for some time and is clinically considered to have reversed within 14 days. Excretion is pH dependent.
summary: Tranylcypromine is a nonselective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor used primarily to treat major depressive disorder, including treatment-resistant depression.
